main_text.p: satisfactiones, plusquam Chrysippeo acumine, eruerint, probarintque. VII. Ut quotquot fuêre Interpretes, mirum in modum desudarint in geminihujusce loci cùm ἐξηγήσεις[?], tum ἀνδικώτερα[?].

III. Secundò inter illa reponimus quae habet author de Melchisedeco, ejusque persona & sacerdotio. Nec sanè toto Veteri aut Novo Testamento perplexius quicquam & intricatius. Et benè in hanc rem Hieronymus ad Euagr. Epistol. cxxvi. quae extat Operum Tomo III: Si vas electionis stupet ad mysterium & de quo disputat ineffabile confitetur, quanto magis nos vermiculi & culices, solam debemus scientiam inscientiae confiteri. In quam vis enim partem sese vertant interpretes, vix sese expediunt, δοκὸς δὲ ἐπὶ πᾶσι τέτυκται[?].

I. Nec solvebant nodum qui olim Mel-chisedeciani, nugantes Melchisedecum θεὸν[?] fuisse δύναμιν[?], Christo majorem, si fides Epiphanio Haeresi LV. Lib. II. Tom. I: Mirifica sanè Virtus, quae & alia à Deo, & Deo major, & humana forma, dignitate regiâ, sacerdotali officio, personalibus a-

page.notes: The last word of the page is broken as "a-" and its continuation (probably "liis") is not clearly legible at the foot, so no catchword is given. The Greek words in lines 2 and 3 of the second paragraph and the Greek word "θεὸν" in the final paragraph are uncertain; they are marked [?]. The signature "liii" at bottom right is uncertain. The Greek in the first paragraph (ἐξηγήσεις, ἀνδικώτερα) is uncertain.
